records.tss_name: At the approaches to Puerto Cristobal
records.vts_boundary_basis: No official source defines a VTS area that includes this TSS. Under ACP N-2-2026 (Z2-S6), Cristobal Signal Station coordinates anchorage entry/exit and harbour movements, and vessels must call it at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater. N-2-2026 does not name the TSS or call the station a VTS. ACP's Enhanced Vessel Traffic Management System (Z2-S7) is a scheduling and information database with no stated service area. NGA Pub. 148 (Z2-S8, Tier 3) says the Panama Canal VTMS 'covers the approaches to Colon and its terminals' but gives no boundary. Coverage of the TSS lanes (about 09°28'N to 09°43'N) is not established.
records.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system applies (the only Part I system in the region is GALREP, VRS-0019). COLREG.2/Circ.65 Annex 2 attaches no reporting. ACP N-2-2026 requires a VHF Ch 12 call to Cristobal Signal Station at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater, plus a continuous Ch 12 watch (vessels of 300 GT or more, 100 GT or more with passengers for hire, commercial towing vessels of 8 m or more) until an ACP pilot takes control. That is canal and anchorage arrival reporting, not a separate MRS. The call point lies about 8 NM north of the breakwater, near the inner (southern) end of the TSS, where the inner lane points are at 09°31'N to 09°32.7'N. The breakwater position is not from an official source. NGA Pub. 148 gives different call distances (6 NM and 12 NM), but the current ACP notice takes precedence.
records.evidence_summary: IMO B-IX/19, adopted by COLREG.2/Circ.65 (MSC 93) and implemented 1 Dec 2014, with inshore traffic zones on both sides. ACP N-2-2026 (1 Jan 2026) makes Cristobal Signal Station the point of contact at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater and has it coordinate anchorage and harbour movements. It is called a signal station, not a VTS, and the notice does not refer to the TSS. NGA Pub. 148 describes a Panama Canal VTMS 'covering the approaches to Colon' without limits. No Part I MRS applies, and the ACP arrival call is canal arrival reporting. This matches the project treatment of TSS-0176 (Gulf of Panama, Flamenco Signal Station).
records.source_date: COLREG.2/Circ.65 23 May 2014; ACP N-2-2026 and N-3-2026 1 Jan 2026; NGA Pub. 148 19th Ed 2025 (updated 4 Sep 2026)
records.unresolved_issue: It is not known whether ACP (or AMP) operates a VTS-designated service, with a defined area, that includes the Atlantic TSS lanes. NGA's statement that the VTMS 'covers the approaches to Colon' is unbounded and Tier 3 only. The official breakwater position and the exact 8 NM point relative to the scheme are unverified. There is no official list of Panamanian VTS. N-1-2026 (Vessel Requirements) could not be retrieved; the URL returned HTML.
records.vts_leads: Cristobal Signal Station (ACP), Port Entry Coordinator; Panama Canal Vessel Traffic Management System / EVTMS (ACP Marine Traffic Control Unit)
records.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: N-2-2026 re-read and 8 NM call and Ch 12 watch verified. Added: NGA Pub. 148 VTMS lead and its conflicting call distances, and the ACP EVTMS described as a data system

records.vts_boundary_basis: No source names a VTS covering the scheme. NGA Pub. 155 para 4.15 notes the TSS with no VTS text. NGA Pub. 120 lists the Russian Pacific VTS (Zaliv Petra Velikogo, Nakhodka, Vladivostok, Zaliv Aniva, Vanino, Petropavlovsk-Kamchatskiy, Magadan; VTMS at Nevelsk and Okhotsk), and none is in the Kuril Islands. Severo-Kuril'skiy, about 45 NM NE on Vtoroy Kuril'skiy Proliv, has only Port Control (VHF 11/16) and no VTS (NGA Pub. 155 para 4.6).
records.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system applies (BARENTS SRS, VRS-0009, covers the Barents area only; the Part I inventory has nothing in the NW Pacific apart from Chengshan Jiao, VRS-0022, in China). COLREG.2/Circ.27 and Russian Government Order 1226-r (2006) set lanes and directions only, with no reporting. NGA Pub. 155 records no reporting for the strait.
records.evidence_summary: IMO B-X/1 (Chetvertyy Kuril'skiy Proliv), amended by COLREG.2/Circ.27 (MSC 52), in effect 4 Aug 1986. Separation zone 50°05.3'N 154°34.0'E to 49°43.8'N 155°14.2'E, with a 2-mile lane each side. Russian Order 1226-r (2 Sep 2006) repeats it as national scheme No. 13 with no reporting or VTS provision. NGA Pub. 155 and Pub. 120 show no VTS or reporting. Pub. 120 recommended tracks 3, 4, 7 and 8 lead to or from this TSS. No Part I MRS applies.
records.source_date: COLREG.2/Circ.27 1 Apr 1986; Order 1226-r 2 Sep 2006; NGA Pub. 155 16th Ed 2026 (updated 4 Sep 2026); NGA Pub. 120 15th Ed 2025 (updated 28 Aug 2026)
records.unresolved_issue: There is no official Russian complete list of VTS (for example from Rosmorflot/Mintrans or seaport obligatory regulations), so VTS absence cannot be confirmed. The Order 1226-r text was read on a third-party host only.
records.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: no VTS and no SRS; Severo-Kuril'skiy has Port Control only, and it is on the Second, not the Fourth, Kuril Strait

sources.supports: National scheme No. 12 Proliv Bussol' and No. 13 Fourth Kuril Strait, with geometry matching the IMO schemes; the text sets lanes and directions only, with no VTS or reporting provision. Third-party reproduction of an official instrument; not verified on pravo.gov.ru.
sources.passage: Схема разделения движения № 13. Четвертый Курильский пролив (Курильские острова). Схема разделения движения включает две полосы движения, разделенные зоной

sources.title: Pub. 155 Sailing Directions (Enroute) East Coast of Russia
sources.supports: Notes the IMO TSS in Chetvertyy Kuril'skiy Proliv and in Proliv Bussol' with no VTS or reporting text (VTS are described elsewhere in the volume for Petropavlovsk-Kamchatskiy, Magadan, Zaliv Aniva, Vanino, Zaliv Petra Velikogo). Severo-Kuril'skiy (on Vtoroy Kuril'skiy Proliv, not the Fourth Strait) has only Port Control and pilots.
sources.passage: An IMO-approved Traffic Separation Scheme lies in the waters of Chetvertyy Kuril'sky Proliv and may best be seen on the appropriate chart.

sources.title: Pub. 120 Sailing Directions (Planning Guide) Pacific Ocean and Southeast Asia, Russia chapter
sources.supports: Lists Russian east coast TSS (including Proliv Bussol and Chetvertyy Kurilskiy Proliv as IMO approved) and lists 19 Russian VTS (Pacific: Zaliv Petra Velikogo, Nakhodka, Vladivostok, Zaliv Aniva, Vanino, Petropavlovsk-Kamchatskiy, Magadan) plus VTMS at Nevelsk and Okhotsk. None is in the Kuril Islands. Foreign secondary list, not an official Russian list.
sources.locator: Russia chapter pp.497 to 498 (Traffic Separation Schemes; Vessel Traffic Service)
sources.passage: Vessel Traffic Management Systems are in operation in Nevelsk (46˝40'N., 141°51'E.) and Okhotsk (59°21'N., 143°11'E.).

services.name: Cristobal Signal Station (Panama Canal Authority) [lead only, not a confirmed VTS]
services.centre: Cristobal Signal Station, Cristobal (Port Entry Coordinator)
services.area_description: Atlantic entrance, anchorages and harbour movements. The mandatory call is at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater. No VTS area is defined, and the TSS is not named.

services.name: Panama Canal Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS/EVTMS) [lead only]
services.authority: Panama Canal Authority (ACP), Marine Traffic Control Unit
services.area_description: NGA says it 'covers the approaches to Colon and its terminals' (no limits). ACP describes EVTMS as its operational database for VUMPA pre-arrival data.
services.operational_evidence: ACP N-3-2026 section 3; NGA Pub. 148 paras 4.40 and 4.44

batch_audits.pass2_evidence_check: No positive association to verify. Re-read from the downloaded texts: the COLREG.2/Circ.40 Cuban annex pages (PDF pp.141 to 145) and circular items .13 to .19 (implemented 24 Nov 1994); the Circ.20 adoption; NGA Pub. 147 paras 4.1, 4.3, 4.5, 4.18, 4.25 and 5.1; and the NGA Pub. 140 Cuba chapter. Quoted passages checked verbatim. Punta Maternillos was matched to the Pub. 147 'off Bahia de Nuevitas' scheme using the Circ.40 coordinates.
batch_audits.pass3_classification_duplicate_check: No VTS or VRS entity created. Cuban 'control posts' were treated as enforcement surveillance leads, not a VTS. Port arrival reporting (Port Signal Station, Mambisas ETA) was not treated as an MRS. No Part I overlap. The five TSS are separate single schemes, with no parent/child confusion.
batch_audits.unresolved_items: All five: no official Cuban VTS/MRS list or MITRANS/GEOCUBA source was reached, so VTS absence cannot be confirmed. TSS-0209: NGA Pub. 147 paras 4.1 and 5.1 conflict over whether the Old Bahama Channel scheme is observed from control posts.

batch_audits.pass2_evidence_check: No positive association to verify. Re-read: COLREG.2/Circ.40 annex pp.144 to 145 (Lucrecia, Maysi); COLREG.2/Circ.65 Annex 2 (Cristobal); ACP N-2-2026 sections 1 and 3 (8 NM call, Ch 12 watch) and N-3-2026 section 3 (EVTMS); NGA Pub. 148 paras 4.38, 4.40 and 4.44; COLREG.2/Circ.27 (Bussol, Fourth Kuril); Order 1226-r schemes 12 and 13 (text extracted by script); NGA Pub. 155 paras 4.6, 4.15 and 4.29; NGA Pub. 120 Russia TSS and VTS lists. Quotes checked verbatim. NGA Pub. 148 call distances (6 and 12 NM) conflict with ACP N-2-2026 (8 NM); the primary ACP notice was used.
batch_audits.pass3_classification_duplicate_check: No VTS or VRS created. Cristobal Signal Station and ACP VTMS/EVTMS were recorded as leads only, not a VTS. The ACP arrival call was classed as canal/port arrival reporting, not an MRS, consistent with TSS-0176/0177/0178 in the current register. Russian port VTS (Petropavlovsk-Kamchatskiy, Zaliv Aniva, etc.) were not linked because they are far from and do not cover the Kuril straits. The two Kuril TSS are separate schemes. Proliv Urup and 'South of Ostrov Broutona' are national-only schemes, not in the baseline.
batch_audits.unresolved_items: TSS-0211, TSS-0212: as B42 (no official Cuban source). TSS-0213: VTS status and area of ACP VTMS/Cristobal Signal Station; official breakwater position; N-1-2026 not retrieved. TSS-0214, TSS-0215: no official Russian VTS list; Russian NMs/UKHO Annual Notices not checked; Order 1226-r read on a third-party host only.

method_notes: Research date 29 September 2026. The NGA publications (Pubs 147, 148, 155, 140, 120, 117) were downloaded through the msi.nga.mil publications API (stored-pubs listing and download?key=...). Text was extracted with pypdf and searched locally. The IMO COLREG.2 circulars (Circ.20, 27, 40, 65) were read in the Transportstyrelsen compilation PDF named in the legacy lead. ACP notices were fetched with curl. Order 1226-r was fetched from meganorm.ru and its text extracted by script. Searches in Spanish and Russian for MITRANS/Capitanía or Russian port obligatory regulations and VTS lists found nothing usable. NGA Pub. 117 had nothing relevant. mandatory_reporting is 'No' where no Part I system applies, the IMO adoption text attaches no reporting, and no national scheme was found. This follows the current register's practice for the Panama TSS. It is not a claim of authoritative absence of VTS. All ten records stay Unresolved because the VTS side lacks an official complete national list. The NGA VTS lists (Pub. 120 for Russia; no VTS section for Cuba in Pub. 140) are Tier 3 indications only. Suggested follow-up: ADMIRALTY List of Radio Signals Vol 6 for Cuba, Panama and the Russian Far East. Source URLs for NGA use type=view; files were fetched with type=download.
